title: Consecutive Numbers
prompt: Find all numbers that appear at least three times consecutively in the logs table. Return one column named ConsecutiveNums.
expected_query: WITH neighbors AS (SELECT num, LAG(num) OVER (ORDER BY id) AS prev_num, LEAD(num) OVER (ORDER BY id) AS next_num FROM logs) SELECT DISTINCT num AS ConsecutiveNums FROM neighbors WHERE num = prev_num AND num = next_num;
explanation: Use LAG and LEAD to compare each row to its immediate neighbors. If both neighbors have the same num as the current row, that number appears in a three-row consecutive streak. DISTINCT keeps each qualifying number only once.
hints: Order rows by id before using LAG and LEAD.
The current row can be the middle of a three-row sequence.
Filter where num equals both prev_num and next_num.
Use DISTINCT to avoid duplicate output values.
common_mistakes: Grouping by num without checking consecutive order.
Checking total frequency instead of adjacent rows.
Forgetting DISTINCT when a number appears four or more times in a row.
Using only LAG or only LEAD and missing the three-row pattern.
